entries.target: wine:Kosta Browne Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir 2021
entries.value: Kosta Browne Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir 2021 is Pinot Noir from cool vineyards on the Sonoma Coast, near the Pacific, made in a rich, polished style and aged in French oak. At five years it gives black cherry, raspberry, cola and baking spice with a touch of oak, medium-full and smooth in tannin. It suits duck, pork, salmon and mushrooms, and a guest who wants Pinot Noir richer than Burgundy. We pour it at 58 to 62°F in a Burgundy bowl, no decanting. The Sebastopol winery was started by two restaurant workers with tip money they had saved, and it grew into a Pinot Noir house guests seek out.

entries.target: wine:Duckhorn ‘Three Palms Vineyard’ Napa Valley Merlot 2020
entries.value: Duckhorn Three Palms Vineyard Napa Valley Merlot 2020 is Merlot from a rocky alluvial fan on the valley floor near Calistoga, at the valley’s warm north end. The stones drain well and keep the vines lean, and Duckhorn bottles it apart, concentrated and deep: black cherry, plum, cocoa, cedar and a little herb, full in body with firm, velvety tannin. It is for beef and duck, roast pork and mushrooms, and the guest who loves Merlot. We pour it at 60 to 64°F in a Bordeaux glass, decanted thirty minutes ahead. Three palm trees name the vineyard, and its Merlot was in Duckhorn’s first vintage, 1978.

entries.target: wine:Château Musar Bekaa Valley 2003
entries.value: Château Musar Bekaa Valley 2003 blends Cabernet Sauvignon, Cinsault and Carignan from vines at around a thousand metres in Lebanon’s Bekaa Valley. It is made at Ghazir, near the coast, and aged in oak and bottle for about seven years before release. Now twenty-three: dried cherry, fig and spice, leather and incense, silky and wild: our celebration bottle for the Lamb Shank en Croûte. We stand it upright ahead, decant it off the sediment thirty minutes before pouring and serve it at 60 to 64°F in a large Bordeaux glass. Gaston Hochar founded the estate in 1930, and it kept making wine through fifteen years of civil war.

entries.target: wine:Penfolds ‘Grange’ Shiraz 2004
entries.value: Penfolds Grange Shiraz 2004 is mostly Shiraz with a little Cabernet Sauvignon, blended across old South Australian vineyards rather than one site and finished in new American oak hogsheads. Twenty-two years on, it gives blackberry, plum, mocha, liquorice, leather and spice, dense and powerful, the tannin softening into a long finish. It is for big beef at a celebration, prime steak or beef tenderloin, and for lamb. Our sommelier presents it, stood upright ahead and decanted forty-five minutes before pouring, off the sediment, at 60 to 64°F in large Bordeaux glasses. Max Schubert, Penfolds’ chief winemaker, studied Bordeaux in 1950 and made the first experimental Grange in 1951.
